title: codemem, end to end
intro:
codemem is a local code search tool for coding agents. It cuts every source file of a repository into functions, classes and blocks, and remembers three things about each: its **words** (keywords), its **meaning** (an embedding of its code) and **who calls it** (an embedding of its callers and tests). An agent asks in plain words over MCP and gets a short ranked list of places in the code.
This page maps **every file** in the repo onto the parts of the system. Click a box to open it: parts open into smaller parts and finally into files, each with what it does and what it connects to. The **Data flows** tab walks through what happens, step by step, from setting up an agent to a search.
howto:
- **System map:** each box is a part of the system; arrows show what calls or feeds what. Click a box.
- **Inside a part:** its sub-parts (in order, when data moves through them), then its files. Click a file for its description, its main functions, and links to the files it connects to.
- **Data flows:** pick a flow and press Next or Play; the boxes involved light up.
- **All files:** the whole repo as a tree, with a filter.
- Press `/` to search everything: components, files, function names, flow steps.
folders:
- `src/codemem/`: the library, the MCP server and the CLI.
- `src/codemem/languages/`: one tree-sitter spec per language.
- `tests/`: the codemem test suite; `tests/fixtures/` holds small repos it indexes.
- `eval/`: `cmeval`, the evaluation harness, a separate uv project with its own tests, configs, task sets and committed results.
- `docs/`: design docs.
- `scripts/`: benchmark and comparison scripts.

components.name: Coding agents
components.summary: The coding agents codemem serves. Each one starts its own `codemem mcp` process when a session opens and talks to it over **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) on stdin/stdout. The agent sees four tools (`search_code`, `get_chunk`, `index_status`, `refresh_index`) plus server instructions, and decides when to call them, just like grep or file reads.
components.details:
codemem never runs inside the agent: the agent only knows the command line written into its config by {{setup|agent setup}}. Everything else happens in the {{mcp}} process.
- **Claude Code** reads a project `.mcp.json`.
- **Cursor** reads `.cursor/mcp.json`.
- **Codex** reads `~/.codex/config.toml`; codemem prints the snippet instead of editing that global file.

components.name: Your repository
components.summary: The code an agent works on. codemem reads it, never writes to it (apart from the agent config files `codemem init` adds, after asking). The {{service|watcher}} hears every save, and the {{indexer}} re-reads only the files that changed.
components.details: Per-repo settings live in `<repo>/.codemem.toml`. Files are skipped, with a recorded reason, when `.gitignore` excludes them, when they sit in folders like `node_modules` or `.venv`, when they are vendored, generated, minified or binary, or when they are bigger than 10 MB. The index itself lives outside the repo, in `~/.codemem/indexes/`.

components.name: People & scripts
components.summary: Humans and scripts use the same library through the {{cli}}: `codemem init`, `index`, `search`, `status`, `watch`, `mcp`.

components.name: MCP server
components.summary: What an agent talks to. `codemem mcp` builds an MCP server (MCP Python SDK v2, `MCPServer`) with four tools and serves it over stdio. It answers the agent's handshake at once and starts the index work in the background, so a session never waits for indexing to begin.
components.details: The server is thin: each tool calls one method of {{service|CodememService}} and formats the result with {{search|render.py}}. All wording the agent reads (tool descriptions, server instructions, notes) lives in `prompts.py`, at three steering strengths (`none`, `light`, `strong`), because getting agents to use the tool at all is a research question here. Logs go to stderr only: stdout carries the protocol.

components.name: Agent setup
components.summary: `codemem init --agents claude,cursor,codex` registers the MCP server with each agent: it plans the config files to write, shows them, asks before writing, then builds the index.

components.name: CLI
components.summary: The command line for people, scripts and CI. Every command is a thin wrapper over {{service|CodememService}} or the library, and prints text (or JSON with `--json`).

components.name: Eval harness (cmeval)
components.summary: A separate Python project in `eval/` that measures how well codemem finds the code a fix touches, against baselines like grep. It builds tasks from real issues, runs every configured system on each task at the task's commit, grades the returned line ranges against the lines the fix changed, and writes reports.
components.details: It uses codemem as a **library** through its adapter, not through MCP: an update finishes before any search, so there is nothing to catch up on. Systems that differ only in search settings share one index, keyed by `Config.index_settings()`. The labeler that turns a fix into gold line ranges is its own implementation, so a codemem bug can't grade itself.

components.summary: Builds the tasks: imports SWE-bench, or collects fresh GitHub issues and the PRs that fixed them, and labels which functions each fix touched.

components.name: Runner
components.tagline: every system × every task, at the task's commit

components.name: Adapters

components.summary: Turn a system into the runner's retriever interface. The codemem adapter builds or updates a per-commit index and calls `search()`.

components.name: Scoring & metrics

components.name: CodememService
components.tagline: service.py · watcher.py — owns one index: the watcher, the single writer thread, and the catch-up every search does first
components.summary: The one object every front-end drives. It opens the {{store}}, runs the {{indexer}} on a single background **writer** thread (the only thing that writes the index), listens to file events with the **watcher**, and makes every search **catch up** on recent saves first, within 4 seconds.
components.details:
**Why it exists:** an agent searches right after its own edits, so that is exactly when the index must be current, but embedding is far too slow to redo on every save. So updates run in two stages (fast structure, slow meaning), and each search waits for the fast stage of every earlier save and embeds the newest edits itself, up to its 4 s budget. If it can't finish, the answer ends with a note naming the files still pending, so the agent can search again or grep them.
- **Watcher** (`watcher.py`): OS file events via watchdog, batched until saves stop for 0.5 s (2 s at most). A change to `.gitignore`, `.codemem.toml` or the git branch, or more than 2,000 paths, asks for a full check instead.
- **Writer:** runs stage A per batch of paths and stage B in between, in slices; pauses when a search wants the model; saves the search index after 30 s without changes; full check every 5 minutes.
- **Catch-up:** a marker-file barrier proves every earlier file event has arrived, then the search waits for stage A and embeds queued chunks itself.
components.maptag: service.py · watcher.py · owns one index: the watcher, the single writer thread, and the catch-up every search does first

components.name: Indexer
components.tagline: indexer.py — stage A: structure (ms) · stage B: meaning (embedding, in batches)
components.summary: Turns files into what search needs. **Stage A** (one SQLite transaction, milliseconds) finds the files that really changed, re-chunks them, updates their keywords and call links, and queues the chunks whose texts may have changed. **Stage B** builds those texts, reuses any vector it already has, embeds the rest, and stores them.
components.details: The work follows the edit, not the file: a one-character change in a 50,000-function file queues one chunk. The queue (`dirty_texts`) is committed in the same transaction as the structure, so a crash between the stages loses nothing, and each queued row carries a sequence number so a vector computed for an older version of a chunk is never stored over a newer one. `codemem index --verify` rebuilds from scratch in a temporary folder and reports any difference from the incremental index.
components.maptag: stage A: structure · stage B: meaning

components.name: Chunker
components.summary: Parses a file with tree-sitter and cuts it into **chunks**: one per function, method and class, plus blocks of at most 200 lines for top-level code. Each chunk gets a key that survives edits (`auth/sessions.py::revoke_session`), its doc text, the names it calls, and whether it is a test.

components.name: Language specs
components.tagline: one small spec per language (the factory)
components.summary: The chunker is generic; a **language spec** says which syntax-tree nodes are functions, classes, calls, tests and comments. `get_language(name)` is the factory: the registry maps file extensions to one spec instance per language, and each spec loads its tree-sitter grammar lazily.
components.details: To add a language, write one spec here and register it. Languages in one **family** may call each other: C with C++, and JavaScript, TypeScript and TSX (family `js`).

components.name: Python
components.summary: Which Python syntax becomes a chunk: functions and classes with their decorators in range; `if`/`try`/`with`/`for`/`while` wrappers are opened only when they contain a definition; docstrings become doc text, the module docstring goes to the first block; tests are `test_*` names and test files.

components.name: JavaScript / TypeScript / TSX
components.summary: JavaScript, TypeScript and TSX share one spec family (`js`): exported declarations are unwrapped, arrow functions assigned to variables or fields count as functions, `new X()` is a call, TypeScript interfaces, enums and namespaces are handled, and `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` files are tests.

components.name: Go
components.summary: Go: methods are qualified by their receiver type (`SessionManager.ExpireOld`), structs and interfaces are classes, grouped type declarations are split, and `Test`/`Benchmark`/`Fuzz`/`Example` functions in `*_test.go` are tests.

components.name: Java
components.summary: Java: methods and constructors, records, enums and annotation types as classes, and JUnit test annotations (`@Test` and friends) mark tests.

components.name: C / C++ / CUDA
components.summary: C, C++ and CUDA (family `c`): names are found by walking declarators, out-of-line `A::b` methods are attributed to their class, macros, typedef'd records, `extern` and preprocessor blocks, namespaces and templates are handled, and gtest `TEST(...)` macros are tests. A `.h` file is read as C++ only if it uses C++ syntax.

components.name: Rust
components.summary: Rust: `mod` and `impl` are containers whose names become part of qualified names, attributes are in range, structs, enums, unions and traits are classes, and `#[test]`-style attributes mark tests.

components.name: Call graph
components.tagline: links each called name to its definitions
components.summary: Links every called name to the functions, methods and classes that define it, within one language family. A name defined more than 5 times (`get`, `run`) gets no links, since it would connect everything to everything. Deliberately simple, and isolated in `resolve_edges` so a smarter resolver can replace it.

components.name: Texts
components.summary: Builds the texts that get embedded. The **code text** is the code with a short header (path, enclosing class, doc). The **usage text** lists who calls the chunk and which tests reach it, which often describes code better than the code does. Long code texts are cut into overlapping windows, each its own vector.

components.name: Keywords
components.tagline: splitting code and queries into words
components.summary: Splits identifiers into words and also keeps them whole (`revoke_session` → `revoke session revoke_session`), the same way for indexed code and for queries, so BM25 matches both.

components.name: Search
components.tagline: search.py · render.py — BM25 + vectors → RRF → cards
components.summary: Ranks the code three ways and merges the rankings: by **keywords** (BM25 over name, path, signature, doc and code), by the meaning of the **code** and by the meaning of its **usage** (each a vector search). Lists are merged by rank with reciprocal rank fusion (each list adds 1/(60+rank)); ties are ordered by location so every machine gives the same order.
components.details: `render.py` turns results into what the agent reads: short **cards** (location, name, id for `get_chunk`, signature, first doc line, a few lines of code, or the best-matching window of a long function), and the freshness note when something is still pending. The eval counts tokens of exactly this text.

components.name: Embeddings
components.tagline: embedder.py · vectorcache.py — local model, API or plugin
components.summary: Turns texts into vectors (lists of numbers where similar meanings lie close together). The default is the local model `jinaai/jina-code-embeddings-0.5b`, on the GPU when there is one. It can also be any OpenAI-compatible API, a Python class of your own, or a fake hashed model for tests.
components.details: Before the model runs, a vector is looked for in this index (same text, same model) and then in the machine-wide **vector cache** (`~/.codemem/cache/vectors.db`), so rebuilds, branch switches and undos cost no model calls. Vectors from different models never mix: each set is named by its model and the settings that shape it.
components.maptag: local model, API or plugin · cache

components.name: Store
components.tagline: store.py — SQLite is the source of truth · FAISS search index in memory (2 bytes per number) · one writer at a time
components.summary: Everything the index knows, in one SQLite database per repo: files, chunks, keywords (FTS5), calls and links, vectors, the stage-B queue and the settings it was built with. The vector search index (FAISS) is a derived copy kept in memory and saved next to the database; it can always be rebuilt from the stored vectors without the model.
components.details:
```
~/.codemem/indexes/<repo>-<hash>/
├── index.db ........ SQLite (WAL): files · chunks · fts · calls · edges ·
│                     vectors · dirty_texts · meta
├── vec_code.faiss .. saved search index per text type (+ vec_code.json note)
├── vec_usage.faiss
└── write.lock ...... one writer at a time (OS byte lock)
~/.codemem/cache/vectors.db ... vector cache shared by every index
```
Readers never wait for writes (SQLite WAL). Every commit that changes a type's vectors bumps its **epoch** in `meta`; an in-memory index that is behind (another process wrote) catches up by comparing vector ids, since vectors are only ever added and deleted, never changed in place.
components.maptag: store.py · SQLite is the source of truth · in-memory FAISS search index (2 bytes per number) · one writer at a time

components.name: Config & plugins
components.summary: Every setting and its default, loaded in order: built-in defaults, `~/.codemem/config.toml`, `<repo>/.codemem.toml`, then environment variables (`CODEMEM_HOME`, `CODEMEM_MODEL`, `CODEMEM_DEVICE`, `CODEMEM_STEERING`, `CODEMEM_VECTOR_CACHE`). `plugins.py` loads `"module:Class"` embedders and vector backends named in the config.
components.details: `Config.index_settings()` lists every setting that changes an index. The indexer compares it with what the index was built with and redoes only what changed (a new model re-embeds that vector set, a new chunker rebuilds); the eval uses it to share indexes between systems.

flows.name: Connect an agent
flows.summary: codemem init → agent configs → the agent launches codemem mcp
flows.intro: How an agent gets codemem's tools. codemem never runs inside the agent: `init` writes a config entry with a command line, and the agent starts that command itself at the beginning of every session.

steps.title: You run `codemem init`
steps.text: `codemem init [PATH] --agents claude,cursor,codex` (default: `claude`). `cmd_init` finds the repo root (the nearest folder with `.git`) and loads its config, which also gives the **steering** level for the agent-facing text.

steps.title: Choose the command agents will run
steps.text: `launch_command()` uses `codemem` if it is on PATH (a `uv tool` or `pipx` install). Otherwise it falls back to `<this python> -m codemem`, which works through `__main__.py` as long as that environment exists, and `init` warns about it.

steps.title: Plan one change per agent
steps.text:
`plan()` returns a list of actions:
- **Claude Code:** add `mcpServers.codemem = {command, args: [..., "mcp"]}` to `<repo>/.mcp.json`. No path argument: Claude Code starts project servers in the project root.
- **Cursor:** the same entry in `<repo>/.cursor/mcp.json`, with `${workspaceFolder}` as the path.
- **Codex:** only a printed `[mcp_servers.codemem]` snippet for `~/.codex/config.toml`; codemem never edits global files.
Other servers already in a JSON file are kept; an invalid JSON file makes `init` refuse.

steps.title: Ask, then write
steps.text: `init` prints the plan and asks `Write N file(s)? [y/N]` (skip with `-y`; `--dry-run` writes nothing). `--write-agent-notes` also appends a short "Code search" note to `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, worded at the steering level.

steps.title: Build the index (and download the model)
steps.text: `init` then runs the same work as `codemem index`: a full build, which downloads the ~1 GB embedding model on first use. With `--no-index` it only downloads and warms the model, so the agent's first search doesn't wait for the download.

steps.title: The agent starts `codemem mcp` in each session
steps.text: From now on, each time a session opens, the agent launches the configured command, `codemem mcp`, and talks MCP to it over stdin/stdout. Continue with the flow {{flow-session|An agent session starts}}.

flows.name: An agent session starts
flows.summary: handshake at once; index check, watcher and model load in the background
flows.intro: What happens between the agent launching `codemem mcp` and its first search. The rule: never make the agent wait for index work to *start*.

steps.title: The agent launches the server
steps.text: The agent spawns `codemem mcp` with pipes for stdin and stdout. `run_stdio()` sends all logging to **stderr** (stdout carries protocol messages only) and creates a `CodememService` for the repo, which opens the index folder `~/.codemem/indexes/<repo>-<hash>/`.

steps.title: Background work starts
steps.text: `service.start()` asks for a full check of the repo against the index (or a first build), starts the single **writer** thread, starts the **watcher** on the repo (and the git folder), and loads the embedding model and the FAISS indexes in a background thread. None of this blocks.

steps.title: Tools and instructions are registered
steps.text: `build_server()` creates `MCPServer(name="codemem", instructions=...)` and registers `search_code`, `get_chunk`, `index_status` and `refresh_index`. Every description and the instructions come from `prompts.py`, at the configured steering level (`none`, `light` or `strong`).

steps.title: The handshake is answered at once
steps.text: The MCP `initialize` exchange completes immediately. The agent now lists the four tools and reads their descriptions, and from here decides by itself when to call them.

steps.title: The writer catches the index up
steps.text: Meanwhile the writer runs the full check: every file's size and date are compared with the index, changed ones are hashed and re-chunked. On a repo seen before this takes well under a second; the first time it is a full build, mostly embedding.

steps.title: Searches during the first build
steps.text: Until the first build finishes, `search_code` answers with what exists so far and a notice (`index is still being built (N% done)`), or says the index is not available yet if there is nothing to search.

flows.name: An agent searches
flows.summary: search_code → catch up → BM25 + vectors → RRF → cards
flows.intro: Follow the running example: the issue *"Disabled users stay logged in"*. The fix belongs in `revoke_session` (`auth/sessions.py`), which shares no word with the query. codemem finds it through its neighbours: `disable_user` and `logout` call it, and `test_disabled_user_loses_sessions` tests it.

steps.title: The agent calls `search_code`
steps.text: `search_code(query="disabled users stay logged in", k=10)`. The server clamps `k` to 1..50 and checks the optional filters `path_prefix`, `kinds` (function, method, class, block) and `tests` (include, exclude, only).

steps.title: Catch up: have all earlier saves been seen?
steps.text: `CodememService.search` gives itself a 4 s budget and calls `catch_up()`. The watcher's **barrier** writes a marker file and waits (≤ 0.25 s) for its own event: file events arrive in order, so once it is back, every earlier save has been noticed. Waiting paths are handed to the writer.

steps.title: Wait for stage A of those saves
steps.text: The writer applies stage A (structure) for the handed-over paths: milliseconds per file. After this, keywords, names, line numbers, call links and the code `get_chunk` shows are current.

steps.title: Embed the newest edits itself
steps.text: If chunks wait for new vectors (and there are at most 1,000), the search pauses the writer's embedding and runs `embed_pending()` itself, newest edits first, until the queue is empty or the 4 s are up. A one-function edit takes 0.1–0.5 s.

steps.title: Ranking 1: keywords (BM25)
steps.text: The query is split into words the same way code was (identifiers split and kept whole; stopwords like "in" dropped) and matched with FTS5 BM25 over five fields, weighted name 10, signature 5, path 3, doc 2, code 1. The top hit is `test_disabled_user_loses_sessions`; `revoke_session` isn't in the list at all: it shares no word.

steps.title: Ranking 2 and 3: meaning (vectors)
steps.text: The query is embedded once (`embed_queries`) and compared with every **code** vector and, separately, every **usage** vector, in FAISS. `revoke_session` ranks low by its code but 2nd by usage: its usage text says *called by disable_user … tested by test_disabled_user_loses_sessions*.

steps.title: Merge by rank (RRF)
steps.text: Each list contributes its top 50, and each adds `weight / (60 + rank)` to a chunk's score. Ranks are merged, not raw scores, because BM25 scores and vector similarities aren't comparable. Optional kind and test weights apply; equal scores are ordered by location, so every machine gives the same order.

steps.title: Cards and a freshness note go back
steps.text: `format_results` prints numbered cards: `3. auth/sessions.py:19-20  revoke_session  [id 14]`, the signature, first doc line and a few lines of code (for a long function, its best-matching window). If something couldn't be caught up in time, a last `Note:` names those files so the agent can search again or grep them.

steps.title: The agent opens a result with `get_chunk`
steps.text: `get_chunk("14")` (or `auth/sessions.py:19`, or `auth/sessions.py::revoke_session`) runs the catch-up without embedding, then returns the full code with its callers and callees from the call graph. A long class is shown as its outline.

flows.name: A save becomes searchable
flows.summary: watcher → debounce → stage A (structure) → stage B (meaning)
flows.intro: The core of the design: an agent searches right after its own edits, so that is exactly when the index must be current. Every update runs in two stages: a fast one for structure that searches always wait for, and a slow one for meaning that runs behind it.

steps.title: A file is saved
steps.text: The agent (or you) saves `auth/sessions.py`. The **watcher** gets the OS file event through watchdog and keeps source files, folders and deletions; it ignores the index folder and folders like `.venv`. A change to `.gitignore`, `.codemem.toml` or the git branch asks for a full check instead.

steps.title: Saves are batched
steps.text: The **debouncer** collects paths until saves stop for 0.5 s, or for at most 2 s while they keep coming, then hands the batch to `notify()`. More than 2,000 paths at once turn into a full check.

steps.title: Stage A: find what really changed
steps.text: The writer thread takes the batch and runs `Indexer.structure`. `scan_paths` reads and hashes each file; a file whose content hash didn't change is left alone.

steps.title: Stage A: re-chunk and match by key
steps.text: The file is parsed with tree-sitter using its **language spec**, and old and new chunks are matched by key (`auth/sessions.py::revoke_session`): same content and lines → untouched; only moved → line numbers shifted; new or changed → rewritten, with its keyword row and calls.

steps.title: Stage A: relink and queue, in one transaction
steps.text: Only calls that can change are relinked: those made by new or changed chunks, and calls to names that appeared or disappeared. Then every chunk whose texts may have changed is queued in `dirty_texts` with a sequence number, and the transaction commits. Milliseconds in total; the edit is now searchable by keywords.

steps.title: Stage B: rebuild texts, keep only real changes
steps.text: The writer takes queued chunks, newest first, builds their **code** and **usage** texts (long code is cut into overlapping windows) and keeps only texts whose hash changed. Texts have no line numbers, so code that only moved keeps its vectors.

steps.title: Stage B: get vectors, cheapest first
steps.text: For each changed text: a vector this index already has for the same text → the machine-wide **vector cache** → only then the embedding model (outside the write lock, in calls of up to 256 texts, longest first). New model outputs go into the cache.

steps.title: Stage B: store them safely
steps.text: Vectors are written unless the chunk was edited again meanwhile (its queue sequence changed; then it stays queued for its newest version). The in-memory FAISS index is patched after the commit, and the vector type's epoch is bumped so other processes catch up.

steps.title: Housekeeping
steps.text: After 30 s without changes the FAISS files are written to disk (not on every save: on a big repo that would block searches for seconds). A safety full check runs every 5 minutes, or every 10 s when file events don't work. A failed stage A is retried and shown in `index_status`.

flows.name: Build an index from scratch
flows.summary: codemem index: walk → chunk → link → embed → save
flows.intro: What `codemem index` (and the eval) does. Unlike the MCP server, it runs stage A and then all of stage B before returning, and writes the search index to disk, so the index is complete when it returns.

steps.title: Take the write lock
steps.text: `cmd_index` runs `Indexer.update()`, which takes the in-process lock and the cross-process OS lock on `<index>/write.lock` (one writer at a time; others wait up to 30 s).

steps.title: Compare settings with the index
steps.text: The index records `Config.index_settings()`. If they changed, only what that setting affects is redone: a new model re-embeds that vector set, a new chunker rebuilds everything. An unknown change means a full rebuild.

steps.title: Walk the repo
steps.text: List every file in a supported language, respecting `.gitignore`, always-skipped folders (`.git`, `.venv`, `node_modules`, …), default ignores (`vendor/`, `*.min.js`, protobuf output) and config ignores. Binary, generated, minified and oversized files are recorded as **skipped, with a reason**: nothing is skipped silently.

steps.title: Chunk every file
steps.text: Each file goes through tree-sitter and its language spec into functions, methods, classes and blocks (at most 200 lines). One file that fails to parse is logged and doesn't stop the build.

steps.title: Link every call
steps.text: On a full build every call is resolved at once and the whole edge table replaced. Names defined more than 5 times get no links; links stay within a language family.

steps.title: Queue everything, commit
steps.text: Every chunk is marked dirty and the structure commits. From this moment the index is searchable by keywords.

steps.title: Embed in big batches
steps.text: Stage B runs to the end: 512 queued chunks at a time, model calls of 256 texts sorted longest first to reduce padding, vectors from the cache whenever possible. This is nearly all of the build time: the local model does about 8.5 texts a second on an M1 laptop.

steps.title: Save the search index
steps.text: The FAISS indexes (2 bytes per number) are written next to `index.db` with a small note, and the run's statistics are stored in `meta`. If the FAISS files are ever lost they are rebuilt from the vectors table, without the model.

steps.title: Optional: verify
steps.text: `codemem index --verify` builds a fresh index in a temporary folder and compares every link and text with the incremental one; any difference is reported and the command exits 1.

flows.name: Measure retrieval (cmeval)
flows.summary: tasks → systems at each commit → hits → scores → report
flows.intro: How the team measures codemem. The eval calls codemem as a library, so every update finishes before any search, and grades results only by location: the returned line ranges against the lines the real fix changed.

steps.title: Build tasks
steps.text: A task is one issue text (the query), the commit it was filed against, and the gold files, classes, functions and lines of its fix. `cmeval import swebench-verified` takes 50 SWE-bench Verified tasks, balanced across repos; `cmeval collect` builds fresh ones from GitHub PRs merged after a cutoff, with the issue text as it was when the fix was opened.

steps.title: Label the gold lines
steps.text: The fix's diff is aligned to the base commit and each changed line is mapped to the innermost function or class around it, with cmeval's own tree-sitter finder, not codemem's chunker, so a codemem bug can't grade itself. New code that didn't exist before is marked unretrievable.

steps.title: Choose the systems
steps.text: A TOML config lists `[[system]]` tables: codemem with given signals and weights, grep baselines. Systems with the same index settings share one index.

steps.title: Check out each task's commit
steps.text: `cmeval run` groups tasks by repo and orders them by commit time. A worktree is moved to each task's base commit, and its HEAD is checked before any index or search, so no future code leaks in.

steps.title: Build or update the index
steps.text: The first system of an index group builds (`CodememService.update(full=True)`), later tasks update incrementally, so only changed files re-embed. The adapter records seconds, size, chunks and items re-embedded.

steps.title: Search and record the hits
steps.text: After an untimed warm-up, each system searches with the issue text (k = 50); the time, and each hit's location and the exact text an agent would read, are written to `<system>.jsonl`.

steps.title: Score
steps.text: `cmeval score` grades hits at file, class and function level (function: same path and line overlap ≥ 0.5), computes recall, precision, success and MRR at several k, tokens until the first right answer (Anthropic token counts), and latency and index costs.

steps.title: Report and compare
steps.text: `cmeval report` writes `report.md` with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired Wilcoxon tests against a baseline, Holm-corrected over the pre-registered primary tests. `cmeval compare` checks that an updated index gives the same results as one rebuilt from scratch.

steps.title: Watch long jobs
steps.text: Long jobs write a status file every 2 s; `cmeval dashboard` serves a read-only local page (127.0.0.1:8765) with live progress.

eval/src/cmeval/adapters/grep.py.summary: The offline grep baseline: ripgrep for keywords taken from the issue, files ranked by total match count (granularity 'file'), plus shared rg helpers used by grep_fn.
eval/src/cmeval/adapters/grep.py.details: Every rg call uses `--no-config --fixed-strings --ignore-case --path-separator / --no-messages --null`, stdin from /dev/null and an explicit path, so results do not depend on the user's ripgrep config or OS; exit code 1 means no match and exit 2 with no output raises. There is no index: build/update just remember the repo and return a zero-second IndexReport, and all grep systems share one index_key (NO_INDEX_KEY). search extracts up to 20 keywords, counts matches per file with `--count-matches` (respects .gitignore, skips hidden/binary), ranks by count then path, and makes each hit's text from up to max_lines (10) matching lines per file in `path:line:content` form, with long lines cut at 300 bytes like `rg --max-columns`. The first hit's extra records the keywords.

eval/src/cmeval/adapters/grep_fn.py.summary: grep-fn: the grep baseline plus the step an agent takes next, mapping each matching line to its innermost function so grep can be graded at function level (granularity 'line').
eval/src/cmeval/adapters/grep_fn.py.details: It takes the top_files (50) files by grep ranking, gets their matching lines (whole lines, no column cut, for counting), parses each file with labels.find_definitions (cached by path, mtime and size, cleared on build), and assigns each line to the innermost named function; matches outside functions or in files without a grammar are dropped. Defaults reproduce the naive ranking: raw match count, then file rank, then start line. Four options (used by grep-fn-plus): `types` limits rg file types (e.g. ['py']); `weighting='idf'` ranks files and functions by the sum of log(N/(1+df))+1 over the distinct keywords they contain (one rg call per keyword in an 8-thread pool); `clean_keywords` drops keywords that look like hashes, paths, URLs or file names (taking 10 spare keywords first); `tests_last` puts functions in test files (patches.classify_path) after all others. Each hit is a function span with its symbol and up to max_lines matching lines as text. Files are read as bytes so a lone \r does not shift line numbers versus rg.

eval/src/cmeval/collect/candidates.py.summary: Collection step B1: turns a repo's merged PRs into candidates (a PR, its one linked issue, and the query) and records a yield funnel with a drop reason for every PR.
eval/src/cmeval/collect/candidates.py.details: `load_settings` reads a collection config: a `[collect]` table (since, until, min_body_chars default 100, extra_bots, max_code_files default 5, max_code_lines default 200; unknown keys rejected) and `[[repo]]` tables parsed by repo_stats.load_candidates; the config name is the file stem. `collect_candidates` fetches the default branch via REST, searches merged PRs, then drops in order: PRs opened before `since`, bot authors, PRs with zero or several linked issues, links that are missing or are PRs, issues opened after the PR, missing or short bodies (as of PR creation), and leaking queries. Each survivor becomes a Candidate with PR metadata, merge commit, commit oids and subjects (used later to detect rebase merges), issue info, query, hints, link method, and tags body_edited_after_fix / title_edited_after_fix. The Funnel has 13 steps: 8 GitHub steps here and 5 git steps filled by tasks_build. `write_candidates` stores candidates.jsonl and funnel.json; `render_funnel` prints the Markdown funnel tables.

eval/src/cmeval/collect/issues.py.summary: Fetches linked issues with their edit history and rebuilds the title, body and comments as they were when the fix PR was opened, then builds the query and checks it for leaks.
eval/src/cmeval/collect/issues.py.details: Issues are fetched 50 per GraphQL query (sorted numbers, so batches and cache hits repeat), each with userContentEdits (up to 100 body versions), RENAMED_TITLE_EVENT timeline items, and up to 100 comments; a number can come back as a PullRequest or None. `body_at` returns the current body if nothing was edited after the PR's creation time; otherwise it takes the last version at or before that time (or the oldest version), and flags it missing when GitHub did not store that version's text (deleted or null diff, as for edits before about 2018). `title_at` uses the previousTitle of the first rename after that time. `build_query` is `<title>\n\n<cleaned body>`. `leak` rejects a query that mentions the fix PR (`#N` or `/pull/N`) or a 7-40 hex word that prefixes any PR commit or the merge commit. `hints_before` keeps non-bot comments created before the PR (stored, not used in the main eval).

eval/src/cmeval/collect/tasks_build.py.summary: Collection step B2: turns candidates into gradable tasks using the full clone: base commit from the merge type, our own patch, file-list and apply checks, size limits, gold labels, and split.
eval/src/cmeval/collect/tasks_build.py.details: `merge_base` (Decision 7) uses the first parent of a merge commit with two or more parents ('merge'); for a single-parent merge commit with N>1 PR commits whose subjects equal the last N first-parent subjects it walks back N commits ('rebase'); otherwise the first parent ('squash'). Tasks get id `<owner>__<name>-<pr>`, source 'fresh', split from assign_split, and extra tags such as link_method, fix_opened_at, n_code_files, code_lines_changed, gold_languages, gold_all_python, max_gold_file_bytes/lines and repo_py_files (cached per base commit). `write_task_set` sorts tasks by repo, merge time, id, saves them, and writes the .meta.json with settings, cmeval git, labeler, funnel steps, per-repo counts/link methods/drop reasons, and stats.

eval/src/cmeval/compare.py.summary: `cmeval compare`: the update-vs-rebuild check, comparing two scored runs of the same tasks (one with --index-mode update, one with rebuild) to show that incremental updates find the same code as fresh builds.
eval/src/cmeval/compare.py.details: Both runs must have the same tasks sha256, the same system names in order, and the same k; the tasks file is sha256-checked. For each system and each shared scored task, the top-10 hit sets are compared by location (path, start, end), never by text, since codemem card text includes chunk ids that differ by design. A system passes if at least 95% of tasks have the same top 10 and every metric mean differs by less than 0.01 (token metrics by less than 1% relative); a metric present in one run only also fails. Each differing hit gets a hint: 'stale' if its file or lines do not exist at that commit (a real update bug), 'near tie' if it is within rank 20 in the other run with a score within 1% of rank 10 there, else 'check'. It warns if the runs are not one update and one rebuild, use different codemem commits, or had uncommitted code, and writes compare-<run B>.md into run A's folder.

It counts api_calls, cache_hits and retries for the CLI and dashboard.

eval/src/cmeval/labels.py.summary: Computes gold labels: which files, classes and functions a fix changed, using cmeval's own tree-sitter definition finder (not codemem's chunker, so a tool is never graded with its own ruler).
eval/src/cmeval/labels.py.details: Only Python has a grammar table (function_definition, class_definition, decorated_definition as wrapper so decorators are inside the span); other languages get file-level gold and `partial_labels`. For each changed code file, a non-blank removed/changed base line goes to the innermost function and innermost class containing it; added lines are placed in the fixed file and assigned to the innermost function/class there that also exists in the base (matched by kind + dotted symbol, k-th duplicate to k-th), so a new method after method A counts for the class, not A. A change outside every function sets module_level_change; if the fixed file cannot be parsed, insertions fall back to the base side (definition containing both L and L+1). Added files and definitions new in the fixed file go to `unretrievable`. A file with a parse error at base gives partial labels. Tags returned: n_gold_files/classes/functions, module_level_change, partial_labels, hunks_moved. `identifier_in_query` decides whether the query names a gold function, class (dunders only as Class.__init__) or file, for the 'easy for grep' grouping. LABELER_VERSION is cmeval-labels/3.

eval/src/cmeval/metrics/matching.py.details: File level: a hit matches a gold file if the paths are equal, and ranks are over unique paths in order of first appearance (`file_units`). Class/function level: a hit matches a gold span if it is in the same file, has line numbers, and either lies fully inside the span or has line IoU (shared lines / lines covered by either) at or above the threshold; ranks are over raw hits. `excluded` returns 'file-granularity system' for class/function levels of file-only systems, 'partial labels' for tasks tagged partial_labels below file level, and 'no gold at this level' when the level has no gold, so these are never scored as 0.

eval/src/cmeval/metrics/stats.py.summary: Standard-library statistics for the report: percentile bootstrap intervals, the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test matching scipy's defaults, and Holm correction.
eval/src/cmeval/metrics/stats.py.details: Bootstrap uses 10,000 resamples with seed 20261023; the resample index sets are generated from a string seed (independent of PYTHONHASHSEED), cached per n, and stored as compact arrays. `quantile` interpolates linearly like numpy. Paired differences are rounded to 9 digits so float noise is not counted as a difference. Wilcoxon drops zeros, ranks absolute differences with average ranks for ties, and uses the exact distribution when n <= 50 with no ties or zeros, or n <= 13 in any case; otherwise a normal approximation with tie correction and no continuity correction. All-zero differences give p = 1. `holm` returns step-down adjusted p-values in input order and treats a missing p as 1 so the family size stays fixed.

eval/src/cmeval/metrics/tokens.py.summary: Token cost of hits: counts each hit text with Anthropic's count_tokens for the agent-study model (minus the fixed request overhead), caches counts in SQLite, and computes tokens_to_first and recall@budget.
eval/src/cmeval/metrics/tokens.py.details: DEFAULT_MODEL is claude-opus-5-5. The API key comes from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or, on macOS, the Keychain entry anthropic-api-key; with no key, scoring stops rather than silently estimating. `--tokens estimate` uses ceil(len/3.5) and is marked as never reportable. AnthropicCounter stores counts in CMEVAL_HOME/token-cache/<model>.sqlite keyed by the text's sha256, measures the overhead once as count('a') - 1 and caches it, and counts missing texts with 4 worker threads behind a shared rate limiter (CMEVAL_TOKEN_RPM, default 3000/min; the SDK retries 429/5xx up to 5 times). Counts are saved as they arrive and committed every 50, and after a failure the already-finished requests are still saved. Whitespace-only text is counted after a leading 'a' (the API refuses it) and 1 is subtracted; empty text is 0. `token_metrics` gives tokens_to_first (sum of hit tokens up to and including the first matching hit, None if not found), found (0/1), and recall@budget<B> for B in 500/1000/2000/4000/8000 using whole hits only.

eval/src/cmeval/patches.py.summary: Parses unified diffs: classifies each changed file as code/test/other with a language, finds base-side changed lines and insertion points, and re-applies a one-file diff to its base text like `git apply` to get real line numbers.
eval/src/cmeval/patches.py.details: `classify_path` maps extensions to ~16 languages (including .pyx/.pxd as cython) and marks a file as test if any directory is tests/testdata/__tests__/spec/specs, if test/ or testing/ is at the repo top or directly under src/ (so django/test/ stays code), or if the file name matches a per-language pattern such as test_*.py, *_test.py, conftest.py. Binary files are 'other'. `_touched_lines` records removed lines as changed and an added run not preceded by removed/added lines as a pure insertion after the last base line. `align_file_diff` finds each hunk at the stated position or the nearest exact match (no fuzz), records the per-hunk offset, builds the fixed file, and lists the added lines of the new file; no exact match raises PatchMismatch. `split_lines` splits on `\n` only (not str.splitlines) so form feeds and other separators do not shift line numbers. `split_patch` keeps each file's diff text unchanged in exactly one of code/test/other.

eval/src/cmeval/repos.py.summary: Git plumbing: one bare clone per repo, worktree snapshots (fixed or movable), and read-only queries (file at a commit, diff, parents, tracked files, apply check).
eval/src/cmeval/repos.py.details: Clones go to CMEVAL_HOME/repos/<owner>__<name>.git via a `.partial` temp folder that is renamed when done, with core.autocrlf=false and an info/attributes file `* -text -ident -filter -working-tree-encoding` so checkouts keep the commit's exact bytes (needed because some repos, e.g. home-assistant, commit CRLF files their .gitattributes says are LF). `ensure_commit` fetches all branches and tags, then the sha itself, before giving up. `checkout(repo, commit, name)` makes either a fixed snapshot `<slug>@<sha12>` or a movable worktree `<slug>@live-<name>` that `move_to` steps to another commit, refusing if it has local changes. `read_file` and `diff` read bytes to avoid line-ending translation; `apply_check` runs `git apply --check --cached` against a temporary index so it works in the bare clone without changing anything. All git calls set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and LC_ALL=C.

eval/src/cmeval/retriever.py.summary: The plug: the `Retriever` protocol every search system implements, the `Hit` and `IndexReport` types, and the hit-contract checker.
eval/src/cmeval/retriever.py.details: Retriever is a runtime-checkable Protocol with name, granularity ('file' or 'line'), describe(), index_key(), build(repo, index_dir), update(repo, index_dir), search(query, k) and close(). A Hit is graded by location only: repo-relative path, optional 1-based start_line/end_line, symbol, score, the exact `text` an agent would see (token metrics count it), and a free `extra` dict for debug data. `check_hits` enforces the contract after every search: at most k hits, forward-slash relative paths, a 'line' system must give valid line ranges on every hit and a 'file' system must give none, so a missing range can never silently become a file-level hit. `stable_hash` is a 16-hex-char sha256 of sorted JSON, used by adapters for index_key.

eval/src/cmeval/run.py.summary: The runner behind `cmeval run`: runs every system of a config on every task, stepping one worktree per repo forward through commits, sharing indexes by index_key, and saving raw hits and timings for later scoring.
eval/src/cmeval/run.py.details: Tasks are loaded, filtered by split and optional repos, grouped by repo (sorted) and ordered by the committer time of base_commit, then id; --limit-per-repo keeps the first N per repo. A FileLock on run.lock stops two processes using one run id. If meta.json exists, the run resumes only if tasks/config sha256, split, index_mode, k, cmeval's commit/dirty flag and each system's name, index_key and codemem git sha are unchanged; it appends a session (start time, cmeval git, machine). Per repo it discards any old live worktree `run-<run_id>`, checks out the first task's commit, and for each task moves the worktree and verifies HEAD equals base_commit (leak check) before any search. For each index group (systems with the same index_key) in folder indexes/<run_id>/<slug>/<key>, `_index_group` builds (first member, first time, or every task in rebuild mode) or updates, using cmeval-built and cmeval-started marker files so a stopped build is wiped and redone and a stopped update's row is marked `resumed`; every call appends a row to index.jsonl. Each system's first search is an untimed warm-up ('warm up', k=1); the timed search uses perf_counter, passes check_hits, and appends {task_id, commit, search_ms, hits} to <system>.jsonl. Systems are closed and the worktree removed after each repo; index folders are deleted at the end unless --keep-indexes. Failures set meta status 'failed' with the error.

_run_tasks: main loop over repos, tasks, index groups and systems

eval/src/cmeval/score.py.summary: `cmeval score`: reads a run's files and writes per-task scores (scores.jsonl), means (summary.csv) and score-meta.json for every level, IoU threshold and metric.
eval/src/cmeval/score.py.details: `resolve_run` accepts a run folder path or a run id under CMEVAL_HOME/runs. `run_tasks` loads the tasks file named in meta.json (or --tasks) and refuses if its sha256 differs from the run's, since labels must match the hits. Only tasks finished by every system are scored, with warnings for left-out tasks or a run not 'done'; k values above the run's k are dropped. All unique hit texts are token-counted once (Anthropic or estimate). For each system, task and level (file/class/function) it either writes an 'excluded' row with the reason or computes relevance per hit (file level ignores IoU; class/function at each IoU, 0.5 always first), turns file-level hits into unique-path units, and writes accuracy and token metrics rounded to 6 digits. summary.csv has the mean and n of each metric (plus not_found_share = 1 - found) and latency rows at level '-' where index costs come from the first system of each index group (the one that builds). score-meta.json records the token counter, estimate flag, overhead, API calls, IoUs, ks, budgets and texts counted; the CLI table shows file R@10/MRR, function R@10/MRR/tokens-to-first and median search ms.

eval/src/cmeval/status.py.summary: Status files for long jobs: each run/score/collect/repo-stats job writes a small JSON file to CMEVAL_HOME/status every 2 seconds from a background thread, for the dashboard.
eval/src/cmeval/status.py.details: The file is named `<job>-<UTC start to the ms>-<pid>.json` and holds job, name, argv, pid, timestamps, state (running/done/failed), error, stage, done/total/unit, rate per minute and ETA (measured over the last 5 minutes of this session; work already done before a resume is counted as done but not in the speed), per-part progress, retries, result values and the last 10 log lines. JobStatus is a context manager: on exit the state becomes done, or failed with the exception (also Ctrl-C); `fail()` marks failure when the CLI handles the error itself. Writes are atomic and every write error is swallowed, so status can never stop a job. `prune` keeps the newest 20 finished files and deletes temp files older than an hour; running jobs are never deleted. `is_over` treats a running job as over if its pid is gone (always assumed alive on Windows, since os.kill(pid, 0) would end the process there) or it has not written for 60 seconds. NullStatus is the no-op default used by library functions and tests.

src/codemem/chunker.py.summary: Turns one source file into chunks (functions, methods, classes and blocks of top-level code) using tree-sitter, and records which names each chunk calls. The walker is language-neutral; all syntax knowledge comes from a LanguageSpec.
src/codemem/chunker.py.details: chunk_source() picks the language from the file extension (or the caller), parses the bytes with that language's tree-sitter parser and runs a _Walker over the tree. Each named function or method becomes a chunk spanning from its first decorator/annotation/attribute line to the end of its body; nested named functions get their own chunks with parent_key set, while anonymous functions (lambdas, callbacks) stay inside the enclosing chunk. A class-like type becomes one chunk covering the whole type, plus a 'skeleton' (header, field lines and member signatures, each cut to 200 chars) that is what gets embedded instead of the full code. Code between definitions is grouped into 'block' chunks of at most max_block_lines (default 200) lines; a single statement longer than that is cut by lines, with cut points chosen by content (a line whose crc32 has its 5 low bits clear, once a piece has a quarter of the maximum), so inserting a line only moves nearby cuts. Calls are collected per chunk in first-occurrence order with the line of each first call; calls in decorators count for the decorated function, calls in field initializers count for the class, and classes themselves get no direct calls. Keys are 'path::qualname', with '#2', '#3' for duplicates; block keys are 'path::<block>@<first 8 chars of content hash>'. Files with parse errors are still chunked from what tree-sitter recovered, and the returned Chunks list carries parse_errors=True. Lines are split on newline only (not str.splitlines) so line numbers match the parse tree.

_Walker: generic tree walker that emits chunks for one file
_Walker.module: top level or namespace body; definitions become chunks, the statements between them become blocks
_Walker.members: class or impl body; member definitions become chunks, other statements become skeleton lines
_Walker.emit: builds a Chunk for one definition (range, qualname, kind, class_name, calls, is_test) and recurses into its body
_Walker.attached: comments and decorators directly above a definition (no blank line between)
_Walker.calls_in / call_sites: collect callee names and their lines, skipping nested named definitions when asked
_Walker.flush / block / piece_bounds: group top-level statements into block chunks and cut over-long runs by content-defined boundaries

src/codemem/embedder.py.summary: The embedding layer: a common Embedder interface with four implementations (local sentence-transformers model, any OpenAI-compatible API, a plugin class named in config, and a fake for tests) and a cached factory that picks one.
src/codemem/embedder.py.details: Every embedder returns float32, L2-normalized vectors at the model's full dimension; Matryoshka truncation is left to the store, so changing embedding_dim never re-embeds. Each embedder has a 'key' naming its document-vector space, and vectors with equal keys are reused across chunks, indexes and the shared cache. SentenceTransformerEmbedder loads the model lazily on first use (default jinaai/jina-code-embeddings-0.5b), resolves the device (auto picks cuda, then mps, else cpu; xpu is used only if torch.xpu is available, otherwise it falls back to cpu with a warning) and dtype (auto means float16 on cuda/mps, float32 otherwise), caps max_seq_length, and uses the model's nl2code_query / nl2code_document prompts or built-in fallback prefixes. Rows that come out non-finite in float16 are recomputed in float32. OpenAIEmbedder posts to <base_url>/embeddings in batches with up to max_concurrency requests in flight, retries 429, 5xx and connection errors up to 6 times with doubling backoff (honouring Retry-After, capped at 60 s), and reads the API key from the named environment variable on every request. PluginEmbedder wraps a user class loaded from 'module:Class', checks that it subclasses Embedder, and normalizes its output. Both real embedders keep an LRU cache of the last 512 query vectors. make_embedder() caches instances by settings; a model named 'fake' or 'fake:<dim>' always wins (default dim 64), then a plugin, then the remote API, then the local model.

src/codemem/indexer.py.summary: Runs index updates, both the first full build and incremental ones: finds changed files, re-chunks them, applies the chunk changes and call links (stage A), then embeds the queued texts (stage B). Also checks that an incremental index equals a fresh build.
src/codemem/indexer.py.details: Stage A, structure(), runs under an in-process write lock plus the cross-process write.lock file and in one SQLite transaction. It compares the stored index settings with the config: a changed setting outside the known tiers wipes and rebuilds the index, 'links' (max_defs_per_name) re-resolves every call, and the other tiers mark every chunk for a text check. Files come from a full scan (walk, then mtime+size pre-check, then SHA-256) or from scan_paths() for watcher-reported paths, which always reads and hashes. Each re-chunked file is diffed by chunk key: identical chunks are left alone, chunks that only moved get their line numbers shifted (unless definitions were reordered), and new or changed chunks are rewritten. Only calls that can have new targets are relinked: calls made by changed chunks, and calls anywhere to names whose definition set changed. Changed chunks, the chunks they call, what deleted chunks called and chunks whose callers changed are queued in dirty_texts with a sequence number. Stage B, embed_pending(), takes batches of up to 512 queued chunks newest edits first, rebuilds their texts, and for each changed text hash tries this index's stored vectors, then the shared vector cache, and only then the model, which runs outside the write lock in calls of up to 256 texts (longest first, code before usage). A batch only stores chunks whose sequence number is unchanged since it was claimed, so edits made meanwhile stay queued, and the deadline and stop hooks let a search interrupt background embedding after at most one model call. Files are skipped and recorded with a reason when larger than max_file_size, binary (a NUL byte in the first 8 KB), generated ('Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT' or '@generated' in the first 2 KB), or minified JS/TS (a line over 5000 chars).

Indexer.update(full, paths, save): stage A, stage B until empty, then save the search index files
Indexer.structure: stage A; scan, chunk, diff by key, relink, queue dirty texts, write meta
Indexer.embed_pending: stage B; drain the queue in batches with optional deadline and stop
Indexer._take / _compute / _put: claim a batch and find reusable vectors; run the model; store complete chunks
Indexer._apply_file: write one file's chunk diff (added, changed, moved, deleted)
Indexer._relink: re-resolve only the calls that can have changed targets
Indexer.scan / scan_paths / _classify: decide which files are unchanged, touched, skipped, changed or deleted
Indexer.verify: builds a fresh index in a temp folder and diffs snapshots
IgnoreRules / walk_repo: .gitignore files (root and nested), always-skip dirs and config patterns
skip_reason: binary, generated or minified detection
IndexStats: counters and timings for one update

src/codemem/languages/c_family.py.summary: LanguageSpecs for C and C++ (including CUDA): functions, in-class and out-of-line methods, function-like macros, structs/unions/enums/classes, namespaces, templates and gtest-style TEST macros. Also decides whether a '.h' header is C or C++.

A function's name is found by walking pointer, reference, attributed and parenthesized declarators down to the function declarator; an out-of-line 'SessionManager<T>::ExpireOld' becomes name ExpireOld with scope SessionManager (template arguments stripped). Destructors (~Name) and C++ constructors (name equal to the last scope part) get subkinds. Preprocessor #if/#ifdef/#else/#elif blocks are transparent, and C++ adds extern "C" linkage blocks and namespaces (as containers, '<anonymous>' if unnamed); a template_declaration is unwrapped so the template line is part of the range. gtest TEST(Suite, Name) and similar macros parse as a function named TEST and become a function named 'Suite.Name' with subkind 'test_macro', which marks it as a test. header_language() returns 'cpp' when the first 64 KB of a .h file show C++-only syntax (template<, namespace, class with a body, using namespace, access specifiers, std::, or a ::name( call), else 'c'.

Methods get their receiver's type name (pointer star and generic parameters removed, so 'List[T]' becomes 'List') as a scope, which makes their qualname 'Type.method' and their kind 'method'. A 'type X struct {...}' or interface becomes a class-like chunk with subkind struct or interface, and its signature is written as 'type X struct' or 'type X interface'. src/codemem/languages/java.py.details: Handles .java with tree_sitter_java. Methods, constructors and compact (record) constructors are functions; constructors get subkind 'constructor' and annotation type declarations get subkind 'annotation'. Annotations sit inside the definition's modifiers node, so they are already part of its line range. Enum bodies are opened through enum_body_declarations so methods inside enums are found. A const/let/var declaration with exactly one declarator whose value is a function becomes a function chunk with subkind 'arrow', as do class fields holding functions; an assignment of a function to an identifier or member (exports.f = ...) gets subkind 'assigned'. A method named constructor gets subkind 'constructor'. TypeScript adds abstract classes, interfaces and enums as class-like types and treats 'namespace X { ... }' as a container. src/codemem/search.py.summary: The hybrid retrieval function: a BM25 keyword list from SQLite FTS5 plus one vector list per enabled vector type (code, usage), merged with reciprocal rank fusion and returned as structured ResultCards.
src/codemem/search.py.details: search() is a pure library function; MCP and the CLI only format its output. It decides the signals (bm25 plus each enabled vector type that actually has stored vectors; an explicitly requested unknown signal raises ValueError, a known one with no vectors is silently dropped), builds a ChunkFilter from path_prefix, kinds, languages and the tests mode, and takes max(candidates, k) hits per signal (candidates defaults to 50). bm25_match() tokenizes the query, drops stopwords (unless that leaves nothing), optionally drops very common words for long queries (bm25_common_share, off by default), and ORs the distinct words into an FTS5 MATCH expression. The query is embedded once per distinct (model, embedder, version) and searched against each vector type; vector search is skipped entirely when a filter matches no chunks. rrf() scores each chunk as the sum over signals of weight/(k + rank) with k = 60 and weights 1.0 by default, ties broken by id; _reweigh() then multiplies by test_weight and kind_weights when they differ from 1. _pick_top() fetches k+10 candidates (extended to include a whole group tied with the last one, and tolerating rows deleted by a concurrent writer) and orders exact ties by path, start line and key so results do not depend on index history. Each card carries a preview: a class shows its skeleton, and a long function whose best code-vector window is not the first one shows that window (best_lines), focused on the lines sharing the most query tokens.

src/codemem/server.py.details: build_server() creates an MCPServer (MCP SDK v2, from mcp.server.mcpserver) named 'codemem' with the package version and server instructions from prompts.py at the configured steering level, then registers four tools whose descriptions also come from prompts.py. search_code clamps k to 1..50, rejects unknown kinds (allowed: function, method, class, block) and unknown tests values (include, exclude, only) with an error string rather than an exception, adds an 'index still being built (N%)' notice while state is 'indexing', and returns 'The codemem index is not available yet' when there is no index and state is empty or error. It calls service.search(..., wait_for_models=False), so a search during model loading falls back to keywords only, and it appends the freshness note (with up to 3 example files from store.pending_paths()) and a 'model still loading' note when relevant. index_status returns the rendered status plus a one-line JSON object with state, progress, chunks, vectors and stale. run_stdio() sends all logging to stderr at INFO (stdout is reserved for protocol messages), creates the service, calls service.start() so the catch-up/first build, watcher and model prewarm run in background threads without blocking the handshake, then runs the server on stdio and closes the service on exit.

src/codemem/service.py.summary: CodememService, the long-lived owner of one repo's index. It runs updates, the background writer thread, the file watcher, the pre-search catch-up and all queries, and every front-end (MCP, CLI, eval) goes through it.
src/codemem/service.py.details: Construction only resolves the repo root, picks the index folder (~/.codemem/indexes/<repo>-<hash>), loads config and opens the Store; no threads start, because the eval adapter re-pins repo_root after construction. update() is the blocking path for the CLI and eval: a full reconcile, every queued vector and the FAISS files written, with errors kept in last_error and None returned. start() is the background path for the MCP server and `codemem watch`: it requests a reconcile, starts one 'codemem-writer' thread (_run/_step), starts the RepoWatcher, and loads the models in a 'codemem-prewarm' thread. The writer is the only thread that applies edits: stage A (Indexer.structure for the changed paths, or a full scan on reconcile) under _apply_lock, then stage B (Indexer.embed_pending) in batches of 64 chunks and model calls of at most 3,000 characters, in slices of up to 5 s, yielding when a search is waiting, new saves arrive or close() is called. Hand-overs of edits are numbered (_received, _applied, _settled) so catch_up() can wait for exactly the edits made before the search, within catchup_budget_ms (4 s), then embed the queue itself, newest first; it skips waiting on a first build or when more than 1,000 chunks are queued and returns a Freshness record describing what is missing. Other constants: FAISS files saved after 30 s idle, a safety reconcile every 300 s (every 10 s when file events don't work), more than 2,000 changed paths become a full reconcile, updates wait up to 10 s while git holds index.lock, and an edited .codemem.toml is reloaded on reconcile (switching vector backend if needed). get_chunk() resolves a chunk id, path::qualname or path:line, waits for stage A only, and shows classes of 80+ lines as their skeleton plus members; status() gathers counts, models, coverage, pending work and, unless indexing, a fresh scan for staleness.

src/codemem/store.py.summary: The storage layer: one SQLite database holds files, chunks, the FTS5 keyword index, calls, call edges, the embedding queue and all vectors, and an in-memory FAISS index per vector type is derived from the stored vectors for search.
src/codemem/store.py.details: SQLite (index.db, WAL mode, one connection per thread) is the source of truth for everything, vectors included: each 'vectors' row holds one float16 vector at full dimension with its chunk, part, line offsets, text hash and embedder key. The search index for each vector type is derived from those rows: by default FaissVectorStore, an exact inner-product IndexIDMap2 over an fp16 IndexScalarQuantizer (2 bytes per number), truncated to embedding_dim and re-normalized, or any VectorStore subclass named in vector_backend. Every transaction that changes a type's vectors bumps an epoch in meta, and in-memory indexes are patched by after-commit hooks, never before the commit. Vector rows are never changed in place (AUTOINCREMENT ids are never reused), so an index that is behind, such as a saved file from before a crash or after another process wrote, catches up by comparing vector id sets, and a missing or corrupt file is rebuilt from the rows with no model. save_vectors() writes vec_<type>.faiss and then a vec_<type>.json note (epoch, dim, count, embedder, backend, file) atomically via temp files. ensure_vec_type() drops a type's vectors when its embedder key changes, while a changed dim setting only rebuilds the search index. vector_search() scores a multi-part chunk by its best part and keeps fetching until the top n chunks are certain, bm25_search() uses FTS5 bm25() with five column weights, and both order equal scores by path, start line and key so results do not depend on index history. Opening an index from an older schema version (current is 3) drops and rebuilds it under the write lock; a newer one raises an error instead of wiping it.

Store.save_vectors: persist changed indexes and their notes

src/codemem/texts.py.summary: Builds the texts that get embedded for each chunk, one builder per vector type ('code' and 'usage'), and splits long code into overlapping windows that are stored as separate vectors.
src/codemem/texts.py.details: Builders are registered by name in TEXT_BUILDERS with the @register decorator, so a new vector type only needs a builder here. The 'code' text is a short header (the file path, and 'in <scope>' when the chunk is nested, written with the language's comment prefix), then the comments above the definition (docstring, or lead_comment for Python), then the code; classes use their skeleton instead of their full code. The 'usage' text exists only for non-block chunks with callers (or, if enabled, recent commits): it names the chunk and file, then 'called by X in path' lines for normal callers and 'tested by X in path' lines for test callers, sorted by path, line, qualname and kind so rebuilt and updated indexes write identical text. Tests are reserved up to half of max_items (default 20) so many normal callers cannot crowd them out, and callers from block chunks are written as 'called at top level in path'. build_parts() returns one TextPart normally; a code text longer than window_chars is split into windows of whole lines overlapping by window_overlap_lines (default 3), sized as evenly as possible, each with the header and a 'part i/n of <signature>' label. Line offsets in parts are relative to the chunk's start line, so code moving down a file does not change its texts, and every part's text is capped at twice window_chars.

src/codemem/tokenize.py.summary: Code-aware tokenizer for BM25 keyword search, used for both indexed text and queries, plus helpers that build a safe FTS5 MATCH expression.
src/codemem/tokenize.py.details: tokenize() finds identifiers and digit runs, splits each identifier on underscores and camelCase (getUserById becomes get, user, by, id), lowercases the parts, and also keeps the whole identifier (lowercased, outer underscores stripped) when it had more than one part, so exact-name queries score highest. Output tokens contain only a-z, 0-9 and underscore, so SQLite FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer with tokenchars '_' does no further splitting. Optional stopword removal drops a short list of English words plus self and cls, and optional stemming strips only a few suffixes (ies to y, ing, ed, es, s, with minimum lengths and never on 'ss' endings). Identifier splitting is cached with an LRU cache of 131072 entries because identifiers repeat across a repo. fts_or() de-duplicates tokens and joins them as double-quoted terms with OR, so words like AND or NEAR stay literal.
key_symbols: tokenize(text, stem=False, stopwords=False): list of lowercase code-aware tokens
split_identifier(ident): snake_case and camelCase split
to_fts_text(text, **opts): tokens joined by spaces, as stored in FTS5
fts_match_query(query, **opts): query to MATCH expression
fts_or(tokens): distinct quoted tokens OR-ed together, or None if empty
STOPWORDS: small stopword set including self and cls

src/codemem/vectorcache.py.summary: A content-addressed vector cache shared by every index on the machine: (embedder key, text hash) maps to a stored vector, so rebuilding or indexing another version of a repo avoids re-running the model.
src/codemem/vectorcache.py.details: The cache is a single SQLite table 'cache' (embedder, text_hash, dim, data) keyed on (embedder, text_hash), stored WITHOUT ROWID. Vectors are kept as float16 bytes at full dimension. The indexer opens it at <CODEMEM_HOME>/cache/vectors.db unless vector_cache = 'off'. Each thread gets its own connection in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL and a 60 s busy timeout, so several processes can share the file. Lookups go in slices of 500 hashes, and writes use INSERT OR IGNORE inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. A failed write is logged and rolled back but never breaks an index update, because the cache only saves work; an index still keeps its own copy of every vector. close() closes only the calling thread's connection and those of finished threads, never one a running thread may be using.
key_symbols: VectorCache(path): the shared SQLite cache
VectorCache.get_many(embedder, hashes): cached vectors by text hash
VectorCache.put_many(embedder, hashes, vecs): best-effort insert
VectorCache.count(embedder=None): number of cached vectors

src/codemem/watcher.py.summary: Turns operating-system file events (via watchdog) into debounced batches of changed repo-relative paths for the service. It also provides a barrier so a search can confirm every earlier save has been seen.
src/codemem/watcher.py.details: The watcher only notices changes; CodememService decides when to index. RepoWatcher schedules a recursive watchdog Observer on the repo root, plus a non-recursive one on the git folder when it lives outside the root (a worktree or submodule whose .git is a 'gitdir:' file). seen() ignores 'opened' and 'closed_no_write' events and directory 'modified' events, skips the index folder and ALWAYS_SKIP_DIRS (.git, venv, node_modules, __pycache__, build, dist and so on), and turns changes to .gitignore or .codemem.toml, or to git's HEAD, packed-refs or refs/ (branch switch, pull, reset), into a full-reconcile request. Otherwise it forwards folders, files with a supported source extension, and paths that no longer exist. Debouncer collects paths and fires once no new event arrived for debounce_ms (500 ms), or at most max_wait_ms (2,000 ms) after the first, so a long burst of saves cannot postpone indexing forever; flush() lets a search take the collected paths at once. barrier() writes an empty marker file named codemem-barrier-<pid>-<random> into the git folder (or a hidden one in the repo root without git) and waits up to 0.25 s for its own event, which proves every earlier event has arrived because events come in order; it returns True on an OSError so it never blocks. git_busy() reports whether .git/index.lock exists (a checkout, merge or rebase in progress).
key_symbols: RepoWatcher(root, on_change, debounce_ms=500, max_wait_ms=2000, skip=()): the observer and event filter
RepoWatcher.seen(raw, is_dir): classifies one event path (barrier marker, git ref, config/ignore change, source file)
RepoWatcher.barrier(timeout=0.25): marker-file round trip proving earlier events arrived
RepoWatcher.pending(): take collected paths now (debouncer flush)
Debouncer(delay, fn, max_wait): quiet-period batching with a maximum wait
_Handler.on_any_event: watchdog handler forwarding src and dest paths
git_dir(root): the git folder, following a .git file's gitdir: pointer
git_busy(root): True while .git/index.lock exists

tests/test_tokenize.py.details: Pins down that snake_case and camelCase identifiers are split into parts while also keeping the whole lower-cased identifier (revoke_session -> revoke, session, revoke_session), and that a single word is not duplicated. Covers acronym splitting (HTTPServerError, parseHTML5Doc), punctuation/dot splitting, and stripping of leading/trailing underscores. Stemming and stopword removal are opt-in and off by default. fts_match_query must quote every term, OR them together, neutralise FTS syntax such as AND, NEAR(), *, ^col: and -, dedupe terms, and return None when nothing usable remains.

overview.name: The big picture
overview.intro: From an agent's first MCP call to a ranked answer, in five steps. Press **Next** (or →) to walk through it.

steps.label: Connect
steps.title: The agent connects over MCP
steps.say: A coding agent such as Claude Code starts `codemem` as an MCP server and talks to it over stdio.
points: The handshake is answered at once; loading the model and catching up on the repo run in the background.
Every call goes to one object, **CodememService**. It owns the index, the file watcher and the one writer thread.

steps.label: Index
steps.title: Index: stage A reads the structure
steps.say: When a file is saved, the watcher notices and the writer updates the index's structure.
points: tree-sitter cuts each file into functions, classes and blocks of top-level code.
Calls are linked by name: who calls what, and which tests reach it.
Only what changed is redone. Chunks whose meaning may have changed are queued for stage B.

steps.label: Embed
steps.title: Embed: stage B adds the meaning
steps.say: Each chunk gets two texts, and an embedding model turns each text into a vector.
points: **Code text:** the code, with its path, class and doc.
**Usage text:** who calls it and which tests reach it. That is how *disabled users stay logged in* finds `revoke_session`.
Vectors come from this index, then a machine-wide cache, and only then the model. Newest edits go first.

steps.label: Search
steps.title: Search: three rankings, merged
steps.say: A search first catches up on recent saves, for at most 4 s, then ranks the code three ways.
points: By keywords (BM25), by the meaning of the code, and by the meaning of its callers and tests.
The three lists are merged by rank (RRF) into short cards: location, name, a few lines.
If the catch-up runs out of time, a note names the files still pending.

steps.label: Store
steps.title: Storage: one SQLite file is the truth
steps.say: Everything lives in one SQLite database per repo. The fast vector index is a copy built from it.
points: Files, chunks, keywords (FTS5), call links, vectors at 2 bytes per number, and the queue between the stages.
FAISS in memory, rebuilt from the stored vectors: exact search in about 10 ms.
Readers never wait for the writer; after a crash or with a second session, the index just catches up.
